headline: SpaceX's Starship goes orbital, deploying first next-gen Starlinks
summary: On its 14th test flight, Starship achieved orbital velocity for the first time and successfully deployed 26 next-generation Starlink satellites.
details: SpaceX's Starship achieved orbital velocity for the first time on its 14th test flight. Crucially, it also successfully deployed 26 of the company's newest generation of Starlink broadband satellites. These flat-packed satellites are too large to fit inside SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9 rocket.

The 407-foot-tall (124-meter) rocket launched from Starbase, Texas, with 33 methane-fueled Raptor engines generating up to 18 million pounds of thrust. The Super Heavy booster stage detached and performed a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico.

The upper stage continued its climb, and after a brief deliberation due to one Raptor engine shutting down prematurely during ascent, mission managers decided to proceed with the orbital insertion burn. This was a critical decision for Starship's first orbital attempt.

The selected Raptor engine reignited flawlessly for 19 seconds, adding approximately 204 mph to Starship's speed. This final push allowed the vehicle to overcome Earth's gravity and achieve a stable low-Earth orbit, marking a significant milestone.

headline_marked: [[Nothing Headphone (1) Pro launch with triple drivers]], 46dB ANC, and a dedicated studio mode
headline: Nothing Headphone (1) Pro launch with triple drivers, 46dB ANC, and a dedicated studio mode
summary: These new over-ear headphones feature a unique triple-driver architecture for a spectacular sound experience and are available September 29 for $399.
details: Nothing has unveiled its highest-spec headphones yet, the Headphone (1) Pro, featuring a new triple-driver architecture. Each cup houses a 40mm bass dynamic driver, a precision driver for mids, and an xMEMS driver for trebles and highs, promising a spectacular sound from 20Hz to 40kHz.

The headphones boast a three-stage, 46dB maximum active noise cancellation (ANC), an improvement of 5dB over its predecessor. This is achieved using 10 microphones to effectively filter out ambient sound.

Designed for both durability and comfort, the Headphone (1) Pro features an aluminum frame, titanium hanger, and scratch-resistant glass on the cups. Softer ear cushions made from fake leather and nylon fabric, along with an 8mm silicon baffle, ensure an improved seal.

An unusual studio mode, developed in partnership with Metropolis Studios, allows a physical button to switch to a flat EQ for critical listening. The headphones are also Hi-Res Audio certified, include spatial audio, and feature an IP52 dust and water resistance rating.
Battery life is rated at approximately 30 hours with ANC on, extending to 68 hours with ANC off. A quick five-minute charge provides two hours of listening time.
Weighing 327 grams, the Headphone (1) Pro are lighter than the original but still heavier than some competitors. They are available in silver or grey for $399, starting September 29.
